subject: Operational Safeguards for Private VPC: BYOK Handover & Subprocessor Notification
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 09:10:00 +0100
Subject: Private deploy - BYOK handover and subprocessor notice

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we move toward the Private VPC pilot, Legal asked me to confirm a few operational points so we can finalize the DPA annex:

- Exact BYOK handover flow (customer key import vs. escrow) and evidence we will receive after handover.
- List of subprocessors that will have any visibility into metadata or operator telemetry during onboarding.
- Breakglass operator access windows and audit trail retention periods (what gets logged, where logs are stored, and how they are shared).
- Any planned cross-border processing for operator support (we need to confirm EU-only).

I've attached our baseline subprocessor register and a redline of the proposed annex (high level). Can you confirm if Redwood will accept the following minimums: customer-kept CMK with optional escrow, operator-access limited to named accounts with approval windows, and SOC2-type evidence for each access event?

We'd like to get contract language agreed this week so Procurement can start the DocuSign flow.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Liu
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Health
Attachments: subprocessor-register-2028-07.csv (CSV), acme-annex-redline.docx (referenced)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 11:28:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy - BYOK handover and subprocessor notice

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; will attach a concise Annex we propose (PDF) for redline. Priya and Irene are looped in for legal/ops specifics.

1) BYOK handover:
   - Primary path: customer imports CMK into the customer's HSM/managed KMS in the VPC; Redwood never receives the unwrapped key.
   - Escrow/optional path: customer may elect to escrow a wrapped key (encrypted with their public RSA) to an HSM-backed escrow vault controlled by the customer. Escrow release requires two customer approvals + ops supervisor signature (audit recorded).
   - Evidence: import/escrow receipts, KMS key IDs, and the envelope encryption metadata are exported as signed JSON receipts. We will provide these artifacts (signed, timestamped) as part of onboarding.

2) Subprocessors:
   - We will provide the current subprocessor register (attached) and commit to 30-day notice before onboarding any new subprocessor with telemetry access.
   - For the Private VPC pilot, operator roles that might touch telemetry are limited to our EU-based support cluster (list provided). No third-party service providers will have direct access to customer telemetry without explicit approval.

3) Breakglass & logs:
   - Breakglass: emergency access is gated by a 3-person approval workflow (customer approver + Redwood on-call lead + RVP security). Each access event is logged; session recordings are kept for 90 days by default and 365 days on request (longer retention is an add-on).
   - Logs: operator actions, keystore API calls, and session metadata are written to the customer-owned logging bucket in the VPC; a signed digest is also pushed to our control-plane logging service for tamper-evident timelines.

4) Cross-border processing:
   - For EU customers choosing EU region, operator support is routed to EU support pods by default. We will not transfer operator sessions to non-EU regions unless you approve a specific support exception in writing.

I'll attach 'annex-byok-handover-v1.2.pdf' with proposed contract wording and the up-to-date subprocessor register. If that looks good, Irene can produce a short redline addressing the legal language you flagged.

Next steps: please confirm whether Acme wants the escrow option enabled for the pilot; if so we'll include brief escrow CLAs in the annex for signature. Also indicate the procurement timeline for DocuSign.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
Attachments: annex-byok-handover-v1.2.pdf (PDF), subprocessor-register-2028-07.csv (CSV)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmehealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 14:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy - BYOK handover and subprocessor notice

Sarah — quick legal/ops clarifications and a small wording suggestion for the annex:

- "Evidence" definition: we propose the annex include a short appendix that enumerates the exact artifacts (KMS key id, wrapped-key envelope, signed import receipt, CID of escrow envelope). That avoids open-ended phrasing in the DPA.
- Retention: Redwood will retain operator session metadata for 90 days by default; any request for extended retention (365 days) should be captured via the SLAs addendum and priced.
- Subprocessor notices: we can accept a 30-day notice for any subprocessor change; for subprocessors that will receive telemetry we will require mutual security assessments (questionnaire + sample audit) before activation.
- Breakglass approvals: recommend adding "customer approver" definition (job title/email list) in the annex to avoid operational friction.

I've prepared a short redline that: (a) defines evidence artifacts; (b) adds a clause about mutual assessment for telemetry subprocessors; (c) clarifies escrow release approval mechanics. I'm fine to send that over if Acme legal wants it.

Also: Priya, if Acme chooses escrow we should confirm the KMS algorithms we support and whether the escrow HSM needs FIPS-140-2 level 3 (they asked). I've noted that in the draft.

Irene
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

Vivek/Irene — this is very helpful, thanks. A few quick confirmations from Acme Legal Ops side:  

- We want the escrow path enabled for the pilot (keep it as optional). Please add the exact HSM levels you support to the annex (FIPS requirement).
- The evidence appendix you mentioned is perfect — please send the redline and we'll mark up the small phrasing updates we need.
- On subprocessors: the 30-day notice is acceptable; for any telemetry subprocessors we will require the mutual security assessment.
- Breakglass: please add a sample approval flow with email examples so our SOC team can map roles to internal approvers.

Procurement timeline: we aim to complete the DocuSign sign-off by EOD Friday next week (2028-08-02). Please populate the DocuSign envelope (link below) with the annex redline when ready.

DocuSign: https://app.redwood.example/docusign/ENVELOPE-54321
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/ACME-98

I'll await the redline and the annex with the HSM/FIPS detail. Thanks again for the rapid turnaround — this helps unblock our pilot kickoff.

Best,
Sarah
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Health
